input: nums is a nonempty list of integers, excluding bool, and k is an integer with 1 <= k <= the number of distinct values. Python integer arithmetic is exact. The paired JavaScript domain additionally requires safe-integer input values and len(nums) <= 4294967294. The integer domain does not distinguish signed zero. Inputs outside the declared domain are not validated.
return: Type: fresh list of k distinct integers. Every selected frequency is at least every unselected frequency; compare the selected values without requiring a particular output order. Descending frequency, with equal-frequency values ordered by first occurrence in nums. If a tie crosses k, the earliest first occurrences are selected. Exact sequence equality is expected between these two candidates on their shared domain, independently of order-insensitive problem acceptance.
mutation_aliasing: Input mutation: none. The returned list is newly allocated and never aliases nums. No persistent Solution instance state.
numeric: Word-sized integers for the paired domain; unbounded Python integer hashing and equality have additional bit costs. Values lie in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991] on the shared domain; n <= 4294967294. Signed-zero identity is not distinguished.
complexity: n = len(nums); u = number of distinct values O(n) expected with constant-time dictionary operations; no sorting is performed. O(n): n + 1 bucket lists, u frequency-map entries, and exactly u stored bucket values in total. The output contains k values.
source_accounting: The Solution class, method, dictionary operations, bucket-list comprehension, loops and result construction are all charged as source. No external helper library or hidden source expansion.
